newsitem.title: UK: London gold notches up more losses.
newsitem.headline: London gold notches up more losses.

text.p: Gold prices explored lower territory on Monday after a key support level gave way, opening the way to further selling pressure, dealers said.
During the morning, the market was walking a tightrope at the $385 an ounce support level but shortly after the opening of New York's Comex futures market prices dived.
The afternoon fix came in at $384.60 an ounce, 40 cents lower than the morning level, then prices lost more ground and closed in London at $383.45, down $2.00 from Friday.
Dealers said previously-set sell orders under $385 added momentum to the slide.
"A break below $385 should sent it down to $382," one said.
Others pegged a new trading range at $380-$385, with the bottom end representing the lowest prices seen since gold fell from its six-year highs around $418 touched in February.
Business was very quiet, and dealers said the market was disillusioned by gold's failure last week to rally on potentially bullish U.S. jobs data and U.S.-Iraq tension.
The market would be watching the Comex options expiry on Friday, dealers added.
But one dealer noted that gold was appeared oversold on the charts and may well manage a bounce, perhaps to the $386 area, after dropping much below $385.
"Gold looks horrible, so people are sitting short below the market, waiting to bargain-hunt at the bottom," the dealer said.
Silver followed gold lower, closing in London down six cents at $5.09 an ounce.
But the $5.05 level was expected to provide decent support ahead of the key $5.00 level, they added.
Platinum closed little changed at $393.75, up $0.15 from Friday's London close.
It was holding above $393 support despite a test of that level on Friday following a week and a half of drifting lower on a lack of interest in the market.
"It may have seen its lows last week," a dealer said.
Palladium finished virtually unchanged at $124.75, down 30 cents.
